title: Romance Scams: Following the Network Behind the Profile
summary: Romance scams and confidence fraud cost US victims $929.3M in 2025. See how investigators link reports, payments and crypto wallets to expose the networks.
body_markdown:
## Key Takeaways


- US$929.3 million in reported US confidence and romance fraud losses in 2025, up about 38% on 2024 (FBI IC3).
- £39.2 million lost to romance fraud through authorized push payments in the UK in 2025, up 23% (UK Finance).
- 22,364 IC3 complaints referenced AI in 2025.
- Operation Jackal IV: 39 arrests, 257 bank accounts blocked and US$2.67 million seized in South Africa.
- Linking shared identifiers across reports (phone numbers, emails, wallets) is how investigators move from one complaint to the network.


A romance scam is a type of confidence trick where a criminal uses a fake online identity to gain a victim’s affection and trust, then exploits that emotional relationship to steal money or personal data. For investigators, a romance scam report can be the starting point for uncovering a wider fraud and money laundering network.


Singles Day on 11 November[began as a celebration of being single](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/explainerwhat-is-chinas-singles-day-and-how-is-it-celebrated-4348058) and has grown into the world’s largest shopping event. Both sides of the day attract fraud.[Purchase scams accounted for 71% of authorized push payment fraud cases](https://www.ukfinance.org.uk/news-and-insight/press-release/fraud-report-2026-press-release) (where victims were manipulated into authorizing the fraud themselves) in the UK in 2025, and the search for connection online is exploited just as readily.


A[February 2026 FBI advisory](https://www.fbi.gov/contact-us/field-offices/sanantonio/news/fbi-san-antonio-urges-public-to-recognize-evolving-online-romance-scams) describes how offenders build relationships through false online identities, then ask for money or steer victims toward fraudulent cryptocurrency investments.


The method is well documented and has not changed in years. What has changed is the scale of the losses, and how far the money travels once it leaves the victim.


## The Cost of Romance Scams


The[FBI’s 2025 Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) Annual Report](https://www.ic3.gov/AnnualReport/Reports/2025_IC3Report.pdf) , published in 2026, records 23,159 complaints and US$929.3 million in reported losses in its confidence/romance fraud category during 2025. Losses rose approximately 38% from 2024. The category covers deception involving romantic, friendly and family relationships, so the total extends beyond romance scams alone.


[UK Finance’s 2026 fraud report](https://www.ukfinance.org.uk/news-and-insight/press-release/fraud-report-2026-press-release) puts romance fraud losses through authorized push payments at £39.2 million in 2025, up 23% from the previous year.


For a snapshot of 2026,[Australian Associated Press reported in August](https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/9335746/fast-evolving-online-scams-fleece-millions-from-aussies/) that Australians had lost A$17.7 million to romance scams in the first eight months of 2026, citing Scamwatch data.


The direction is the same in the countries that publish comparable data, and the real totals are higher than the published ones because many victims never report the crime. The growth lies in how convincingly the familiar approach can now be delivered.


## Old Manipulation, New AI Tools


Romance fraud often involves sustained contact. An offender builds trust before introducing an emergency, asking for financial help or recommending an investment platform controlled by criminals. INTERPOL calls this hybrid of romance and investment fraud[romance baiting](https://www.interpol.int/en/News-and-Events/News/2024/INTERPOL-urges-end-to-Pig-Butchering-term-cites-harm-to-online-victims) , a term it has proposed in place of more widely used “[pig](https://securityboulevard.com/2023/10/how-to-combat-pig-butchering-scams-with-decision-intelligence/)[butchering](https://www.cognyte.com/news/how-to-combat-pig-butchering-scams-with-decision-intelligence/) ” because it puts the focus on the perpetrator rather than shaming the victim. Some victims are also[recruited as money mules](https://www.fbi.gov/contact-us/field-offices/sanantonio/news/fbi-san-antonio-urges-public-to-recognize-evolving-online-romance-scams) , moving funds on the offender’s behalf and leaving their own accounts in the laundering chain.


AI can make the deception harder to recognize. The FBI’s advisory describes criminals using it to improve translations, remove grammatical errors and generate realistic images. The scale is now measurable: the[IC3 report logged 22,364 complaints that referenced AI](https://www.ic3.gov/AnnualReport/Reports/2025_IC3Report.pdf) in 2025, including US$19 million in confidence/romance losses with a likely AI nexus.


For investigators, that makes it important to test a claimed identity against independent evidence. A convincing profile or fluent conversation provides little assurance on its own.


## The Network Beyond the Dating Profile


Enforcement results published in 2026 show the organized operations behind some of these crimes. During[Operation Jackal IV](https://www.interpol.int/en/News-and-Events/News/2026/58-arrests-in-global-effort-to-dismantle-West-African-organized-crime-groups) , which ran from November 2025 to June 2026, South African authorities raided seven locations linked to a syndicate conducting romance and investment scams against retirees in English-speaking countries. They arrested 39 people, blocked 257 bank accounts and seized US$2.67 million.


The operation also flagged the growth of Crime-as-a-Service, where criminal service providers move and hide stolen funds on behalf of the scam networks, and a rise in sextortion.[INTERPOL’s March 2026 threat assessment](https://www.interpol.int/en/News-and-Events/News/2026/INTERPOL-report-warns-of-increasingly-sophisticated-global-financial-fraud-threat) describes sextortion being built into romance and investment scams, including through AI-generated content, as part of layered operations that target victims repeatedly.


A separate case reported under INTERPOL’s Operation First Light 2026 involved a money laundering scheme uncovered in Thailand that moved romance scam proceeds through cryptocurrencies and cross-chain token swaps. One suspect’s wallet had processed more than US$122.5 million in 10 months. That is wallet transaction volume, not a verified total of romance scam losses.


The network does not always let go after the first loss. In July 2026 the[FBI warned](https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2026/PSA260720) that criminals are contacting previous fraud victims with fake fund-recovery offers, some posing as FBI personnel and using AI-generated videos and spoofed complaint websites. The victim’s own report becomes the lure for a second scam, which is one more reason to link reports across time as well as across cases.


These cases illustrate why investigating a single profile is only part of the work. Investigators also need to identify the payment recipients and establish how their accounts connect to other incidents.


## From Scattered Reports to a Unified Investigation


[Decision intelligence](https://www.cognyte.com/nexyte/what-is-decision-intelligence/) helps investigators bring information from different sources into a shared investigative view. In a romance fraud investigation, this means connecting customers’ data such as victim reports, online identities, financial accounts, and cryptocurrency transactions to uncover hidden relationships and potential links to wider criminal networks.


[NEXYTE](https://www.cognyte.com/nexyte/) , Cognyte’s decision intelligence platform, supports this work through:


- [Entity resolution](https://www.cognyte.com/nexyte/entity-resolution/) and[data fusion](https://www.cognyte.com/nexyte/data-fusion/) match identifiers across reports, financial and corporate data, cryptocurrency intelligence and other sources available to the agency, so an email address or wallet that appears in two complaints is linked automatically.
- [Link analysis](https://www.cognyte.com/nexyte/link-analysis-software/) and[graph analytics](https://www.cognyte.com/nexyte/graph-analytics/) map how entities connect, showing where separate payments converge on the same recipient or money laundering path.
- AI-based risk models prioritize entities and surface clusters of connected accounts, so analysts know which leads to pursue first when complaints run into the hundreds.
- [Agentic decision flows](https://engage.cognyte.com/s/897e8ae2/agentic-decision-flows/?page=1) guide next steps and automate repetitive tasks, while keeping investigators in control of critical decisions, enabling teams to work on individual scams and organized networks alike.
- A shared workspace with role-based access control lets teams and partner agencies work the same case, which matters when a network spans jurisdictions, as Operation Jackal IV did.


For example, when a phone number from one victim’s report also appears in another case, NEXYTE surfaces the match automatically and links the related account information available to the investigation. The analyst starts from a lead rather than a manual cross-check. Establishing who controls an account still requires corroborating evidence.


The aim is to reduce the time spent processing and analyzing information so investigators can assess the links, gather evidence and coordinate action. Access to the relevant data and cooperation between agencies remain essential. By fusing fragmented intelligence, uncovering hidden relationships, and guiding investigators toward actionable leads, NEXYTE helps expose the broader fraud and money laundering networks behind individual romance scams.
